democratic.summary: Documents support easier union organizing and collective bargaining, stronger labor-law enforcement, strike protections, expanded rights for excluded workers, higher minimum wages, overtime protections, and labor standards in trade.
democratic.caveat: Several examples are retrospective achievements or worker-related facts rather than new policy commitments.

republican.summary: Documents affirm voluntary union participation while supporting state or national right-to-work laws, union financial disclosure, repeal of Davis-Bacon, employer flexibility, workforce training, and selected worker protections.
republican.caveat: The packet combines labor policy with retirement, welfare, immigration verification, and civil-service claims.

dsa.summary: Documents support broad rights to organize, bargain, and strike; labor-law reform and enforcement; union democratization; living wages; worker ownership; job guarantees; and protections regardless of industry or immigration status.
dsa.caveat: Fallback material includes factual descriptions and adjacent employment, pension, and unemployment policies.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Democratic documents seek easier organizing and stronger bargaining and strike protections; Republican documents preserve voluntary unionism while advancing right-to-work, union disclosure, and Davis-Bacon repeal.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Both support organizing and bargaining rights; DSA documents additionally emphasize universal strike rights, union democratization, worker ownership, and a federal jobs guarantee.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican documents emphasize voluntary unionism and right-to-work restrictions; DSA documents seek expansive organizing and strike rights, stronger enforcement, and democratic unions.
